_comment: Offline demo script for 'Build a Leave Management System'. BA attempt 1 is deliberately weak (untestable criteria, invented Workday integration): the Tier-1 judge scores it borderline (3.2), the Tier-2 judge confirms (3.0) and the gate returns RETRY; attempt 2 passes.

persona:pm.objective: Give employees a self-service way to request leave and managers a way to approve it, backed by accurate, policy-driven leave balances.
business_goals: Employees can request leave and see their remaining balance without contacting HR.
Managers can approve or reject leave requests with visibility of their team's absences.
Leave balances are calculated consistently from the organisation's leave policy.
HR has an auditable record of every leave request and decision.
success_metrics: >= 90% of leave requests submitted through the system within 3 months of launch.
Median manager approval turnaround <= 2 business days.
0 balance discrepancies between the system and payroll in the monthly reconciliation.
constraints: No existing HR, payroll or identity systems are named in the request; integration targets are unconfirmed and must not be assumed.
Leave policy rules (entitlements, accrual, carry-over, public holidays) are not specified and must be supplied by HR.
Leave records are personal employee data (and sick-leave reasons may be health data), so they fall under the organisation's data-protection obligations.
out_of_scope: Multi-country statutory leave rules in phase 1.

acceptance_criteria.description: The request form is easy to use.

user_stories.so_that: my team can take time off
I know how much leave I have

non_functional_requirements: Employee and manager data is synchronised in real time from Workday via its REST API.
Approved leave is pushed automatically to the payroll system.
The system should be fast and secure.

user_stories.i_want: to submit a leave request for a leave type and date range
user_stories.so_that: I can book time off without contacting HR

acceptance_criteria.description: Given a leave type, start date and end date, a request is created with status PENDING and its working days are calculated excluding weekends and configured public holidays.
A request whose working days exceed the employee's available balance for that leave type is rejected and the available balance is shown.
A request that overlaps one of the employee's PENDING or APPROVED requests is rejected.

user_stories.i_want: to approve or reject my direct reports' leave requests

acceptance_criteria.description: A manager can approve or reject only requests from their direct reports.
Approving keeps the request's working days deducted from the balance; rejecting returns them to the balance.
A rejection requires a reason, which is shown to the employee.

user_stories.i_want: to see my remaining balance per leave type

acceptance_criteria.description: Available balance = annual entitlement + carry-over (capped by policy) - approved days - pending days for the current leave year.
Balances are shown separately for each leave type.

user_stories.i_want: to configure entitlement and carry-over per leave type

acceptance_criteria.description: HR can set annual entitlement and maximum carry-over for each leave type.
A policy change applies from its effective date and does not alter already-approved requests.

user_stories.i_want: an audit trail of every leave action

acceptance_criteria.description: Every create, approve and reject action is recorded with actor, timestamp, previous status and new status.
Audit records cannot be edited or deleted through the application.

non_functional_requirements: Security: role-based access for employee, manager and HR roles; authentication through the organisation's identity provider once it is confirmed (open question), local accounts only in the pilot.
Privacy: the optional leave reason may contain health data; it is visible only to the employee, their manager and HR, and is retained per the data-protection policy.
Performance: balance lookup p95 < 500 ms for 5,000 employees.
Integration: no HRIS or payroll integration is assumed; approved leave is exported as a file until the payroll system is confirmed.
open_questions: Which system is the source of truth for employees and reporting lines (HRIS), and how can we read from it?
Which identity provider should the system authenticate against?
What are the leave types, entitlements, accrual and carry-over rules, and public-holiday calendars per location?
Does payroll need approved leave, and in what format and frequency?
How should sick-leave reasons (health data) be handled and retained?

components.name: Web UI
components.responsibility: Employee request and balance screens, manager approval queue, HR policy and audit screens.

components.name: Leave Service
components.responsibility: Validates and stores leave requests; enforces overlap and balance rules.

components.name: Policy Engine
components.responsibility: Data-driven entitlement, carry-over and working-day rules per leave type with effective dates.

components.name: Approval Workflow
components.responsibility: Routes requests to the employee's direct manager; records approve/reject decisions.

components.name: Directory Adapter
components.responsibility: Provides employees and reporting lines; initial implementation is a nightly CSV import from HR.

components.name: Payroll Export Adapter
components.responsibility: Produces a file of approved leave for payroll; format confirmed later.

components.name: Audit Log
components.responsibility: Append-only record of every leave action.

persona:architect.integration_approach: No HR, payroll or identity system is confirmed, so every external dependency sits behind an adapter interface with a deliberately simple first implementation: the Directory Adapter imports employees and reporting lines from a nightly HR-provided CSV; identity uses local accounts in the pilot behind an IdentityAdapter that will switch to the organisation's OIDC provider once confirmed; the Payroll Export Adapter writes a CSV of approved leave for manual upload. When HR confirms the real systems, only the adapters change, not the Leave Service or Policy Engine.
persona:architect.data_flow: Employee submits a request in the Web UI -> Leave Service asks the Policy Engine for working days and available balance -> request stored as PENDING and logged in the Audit Log -> Approval Workflow looks up the manager via the Directory Adapter and queues it -> manager approves or rejects -> status updated and audited -> approved requests are included in the next Payroll Export file.

risks.description: Leave policy rules turn out more complex than modelled (accrual, pro-rata, carry-over).
risks.mitigation: Policy Engine is data-driven with effective dates; pilot with two leave types and validate against 20 worked examples supplied by HR before launch.

risks.description: Reporting lines in the CSV import are stale, so requests route to the wrong manager.
risks.mitigation: Nightly import produces a diff report for HR; requests whose manager is unknown fall back to an HR approval queue.
Reason field is optional, access-restricted to employee, manager and HR, and excluded from exports and reports.

adrs.title: Adapters for every unconfirmed integration
adrs.decision: Put directory, identity and payroll behind adapters with file-based first implementations.
alternatives_considered: Build directly against a presumed HRIS API
Wait for integration decisions before starting
adrs.rationale: The requirement names no systems; adapters let delivery start without inventing integrations.

adrs.title: Data-driven policy engine
adrs.decision: Encode entitlements, carry-over and holidays as data with effective dates.
adrs.rationale: HR has not yet supplied the rules and they will change; data changes need no redeploy.

adrs.title: Modular monolith
adrs.decision: Single deployable with clear module boundaries.
adrs.rationale: Small team and modest scale; boundaries allow later extraction.

from datetime import date

import pytest

from leave.policy import LeavePolicy, working_days
from leave.service import LeaveError, LeaveService


def make_service():
    return LeaveService(
        policies={"ANNUAL": LeavePolicy("ANNUAL", annual_entitlement=20)},
        managers={"emp-1": "mgr-1", "emp-2": "mgr-2"},
        holidays=frozenset({date(2026, 12, 25)}),
    )


def test_working_days_exclude_weekends_and_holidays():
    # Mon 21 - Sun 27 Dec 2026 with 25 Dec a public holiday -> 4 working days
    assert working_days(date(2026, 12, 21), date(2026, 12, 27), frozenset({date(2026, 12, 25)})) == 4


def test_submit_creates_pending_request_with_working_days():
    request = make_service().submit("emp-1", "ANNUAL", date(2026, 12, 21), date(2026, 12, 24))
    assert request.status == "PENDING"
    assert request.days == 4


def test_overlapping_request_is_rejected():
    service = make_service()
    service.submit("emp-1", "ANNUAL", date(2026, 12, 21), date(2026, 12, 24))
    with pytest.raises(LeaveError, match="overlaps"):
        service.submit("emp-1", "ANNUAL", date(2026, 12, 23), date(2026, 12, 29))


def test_request_exceeding_balance_is_rejected():
    with pytest.raises(LeaveError, match="insufficient balance"):
        make_service().submit("emp-1", "ANNUAL", date(2026, 1, 5), date(2026, 2, 13))


def test_only_direct_manager_decides_and_rejection_needs_reason():
    service = make_service()
    request = service.submit("emp-1", "ANNUAL", date(2026, 12, 21), date(2026, 12, 22))
    with pytest.raises(LeaveError, match="direct manager"):
        service.approve("mgr-2", request.id)
    with pytest.raises(LeaveError, match="reason"):
        service.reject("mgr-1", request.id, " ")


def test_reject_returns_days_and_approve_keeps_them_deducted():
    service = make_service()
    first = service.submit("emp-1", "ANNUAL", date(2026, 12, 21), date(2026, 12, 22))
    assert service.balance("emp-1", "ANNUAL") == 18
    service.reject("mgr-1", first.id, "team cover")
    assert service.balance("emp-1", "ANNUAL") == 20
    second = service.submit("emp-1", "ANNUAL", date(2026, 12, 21), date(2026, 12, 23))
    service.approve("mgr-1", second.id)
    assert service.balance("emp-1", "ANNUAL") == 17
    assert [a["action"] for a in service.audit] == ["create", "reject", "create", "approve"]

stubbed_stories.plan: Balance screen: expose LeaveService.balance per leave type through the Leave Service API; the calculation (US-3-AC1) already exists in policy.available_balance.
Policy admin: persist LeavePolicy rows with an effective_from date in the Policy Engine; requests keep the policy version they were approved under.
Audit Log: move the in-memory audit list to an append-only table with no UPDATE/DELETE grants for the application role.

deviations: The repository is in-memory in this slice; persistence is designed but not implemented.
The Directory Adapter is represented by the managers mapping passed to LeaveService.
persona:dev.summary: Implemented the Policy Engine (working days, available balance) and the Leave Service with Approval Workflow for US-1 and US-2, including overlap and balance checks, direct-manager authorisation, mandatory rejection reasons and an audit record per action. Every external dependency stays behind the adapter boundary from the design. US-3, US-4 and US-5 are stubbed with plans.

steps: Count working days for Mon 21 - Sun 27 Dec 2026 with 25 Dec as a holiday
test_cases.expected_result: 4 working days; request created with status PENDING and days = 4.

steps: Submit a 30-working-day request against a 20-day entitlement
test_cases.expected_result: Rejected with 'insufficient balance' showing the available balance.

steps: Submit 23-29 Dec for the same employee
Another employee's manager tries to approve
Direct manager rejects with a blank reason
Submit 3 days, approve, check balance and audit trail
test_cases.expected_result: Balance 18 -> 20 -> 17; audit shows create, reject, create, approve with actor, timestamp and statuses.

steps: Employee submits a request in the Web UI
Manager approves it from the approval queue
test_cases.expected_result: Balance reduced by the request's working days and request shown as APPROVED.

persona:qa.coverage_summary: All US-1 and US-2 acceptance criteria plus US-3-AC1 and US-5-AC1 are covered by unit tests that ship with the implementation (see the measured execution report). TC-6 is an end-to-end case for when the Web UI exists.
gaps: No UI exists yet, so TC-6 cannot run.
Persistence is in-memory; US-5-AC2 (immutability) needs the database implementation.

judge:pm_to_ba:tier1.feedback: Objective, goals and metrics are measurable; the PM correctly records that no HR, payroll or identity systems are named instead of inventing them. Minor: name an owner for the leave policy.

blocking_issues: US-1..US-4 acceptance criteria are not testable.
NFR assumes Workday and a payroll push; the brief states integration targets are unconfirmed.
Only one open question; policy rules, identity provider and payroll format are unresolved.
judge:ba_to_architect:tier1.feedback: Acceptance criteria are not testable ('easy to use', 'work correctly', 'is accurate') and the NFRs assume a real-time Workday REST integration and automatic payroll push, although the brief says no HR or payroll system is confirmed. Rewrite each criterion as a checkable condition, add the missing overlap/balance rules, and move integrations to open questions.
Criteria are now testable, integrations are raised as open questions rather than assumed, and every story traces to a goal. Minor: US-4-AC2 needs an example of a mid-year policy change.

blocking_issues: Invented Workday REST integration and payroll push.
judge:ba_to_architect:tier2.feedback: Confirmed: acceptance criteria are untestable and the Workday/payroll assumptions contradict the brief's constraint that no integration targets are confirmed. Retry with measurable criteria and integrations raised as open questions.

judge:architect_to_dev:tier1.feedback: Adapters with file-based first implementations respect the unconfirmed-integration constraint; risks have concrete mitigations; ADRs list alternatives. Minor: state the CSV import schedule owner.

judge:dev_to_qa:tier1.feedback: US-1 and US-2 implemented as designed with tests; other stories stubbed honestly; in-memory repository stated as a deviation.
